title: Psalms Chapter 138 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 138 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 138 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 138.

questions.question: Who is credited with the Psalm in Psalms 138:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 begins with the statement 'A Psalm of David,' indicating David is the author.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:1, with what will the psalmist praise the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist says, 'I will praise thee with my whole heart' in Psalms 138:1.

questions.question: Before whom will the psalmist sing praise according to Psalms 138:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 states, 'before the gods will I sing praise unto thee.'

questions.question: Towards what place does the psalmist say he will worship in Psalms 138:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 says, 'I will worship toward thy holy temple.'

questions.question: For which two attributes does the psalmist praise God's name in Psalms 138:2?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 states, 'praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:2, what has God magnified above all his name?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.'

questions.question: When did God answer the psalmist according to Psalms 138:3?
options: In the day when I cried
questions.correctAnswer: In the day when I cried
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 states, 'In the day when I cried thou answeredst me.'

questions.question: What did God strengthen in the psalmist according to Psalms 138:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 says, 'strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:1 states the psalmist will praise God with his whole heart.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 clearly states, 'I will praise thee with my whole heart.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 138:2, God's name is magnified above all his words.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 says 'thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name,' so the word is magnified above the name, not the other way around.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:3 mentions that God strengthens the psalmist's soul.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 says God 'strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:1 says the psalmist will sing praise before the people of Israel.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 states the psalmist will sing praise 'before the gods,' not specifically before the people of Israel.

questions.question: In Psalms 138, what comes first?
options: The psalmist praises God's name for lovingkindness and truth
The psalmist declares he will praise God with his whole heart
God answers the psalmist when he cries
The psalmist worships toward God's holy temple
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist declares he will praise God with his whole heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 opens with the psalmist saying 'I will praise thee with my whole heart,' which comes before the other events described in verses 2 and 3.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:2, the psalmist praises God's name for which two reasons?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 says, 'praise thy name for thy lovingkindness and for thy truth.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:3, what did God do when the psalmist cried?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 states, 'In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul.'

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 138 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 138 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:4, who shall praise the LORD when they hear the words of His mouth?
options: All the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: All the kings of the earth
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:4 explicitly states that all the kings of the earth shall praise the LORD when they hear the words of His mouth, emphasizing the universal recognition of God's word.

questions.question: How does Psalms 138:5 describe the response of those who praise the LORD?
options: They shall sing in the ways of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: They shall sing in the ways of the LORD
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 138:5, those who praise the LORD will sing in the ways of the LORD, showing their joyful obedience and recognition of His glory.

questions.question: What reason does Psalms 138:5 give for why people will sing in the ways of the LORD?
options: Because great is the glory of the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: Because great is the glory of the LORD
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:5 states that people will sing in the ways of the LORD because great is the glory of the LORD, highlighting the motivation for praise is God's magnificent glory.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:6, how does the LORD treat the lowly?
options: He has respect unto the lowly
questions.correctAnswer: He has respect unto the lowly
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:6 says that though the LORD is exalted, He has respect unto the lowly, showing God's care and favor for humble people.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:6 say about the proud in relation to the LORD?
questions.explanation: The verse explains that the LORD knows the proud from afar, indicating a distance or separation due to their pride.

questions.question: What connection can be made between Psalms 138:4 and 138:5 about the response of kings to God's word?
options: Kings will praise the LORD and sing in His ways because of His glory
Kings will ignore the LORD's words and rebel
Kings will fear the LORD and hide
Kings will build temples to rival God's
questions.correctAnswer: Kings will praise the LORD and sing in His ways because of His glory
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:4 states that kings will praise the LORD when they hear His word, and 138:5 adds that they will sing in His ways because great is His glory, showing a linked cause and effect.

questions.question: Based on Psalms 138:6, what biblical virtue is emphasized by the LORD's respect for the lowly and distance from the proud?
questions.explanation: The LORD's respect for the lowly and His knowledge of the proud from afar in Psalms 138:6 highlights humility as a prized virtue in God’s eyes.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:7 promise will happen if a believer walks in the midst of trouble?
options: The LORD will revive them and save them from enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will revive them and save them from enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:7 promises that even in trouble, the LORD will revive the believer and stretch out His hand against their enemies, showing God's protection.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:8 say about the LORD's mercy and His works?
options: His mercy endures forever and He will not forsake His works
His mercy is temporary and He forgets His works
His mercy is conditional and He abandons His works
His mercy is limited and He ignores His works
questions.correctAnswer: His mercy endures forever and He will not forsake His works
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 138:8, the LORD's mercy is everlasting and He will not forsake the works of His own hands, demonstrating God's faithfulness.

questions.question: A fellow believer feels insignificant and struggles with pride. According to Psalms 138:6, what biblical truth can you share?
options: God respects the lowly but distances Himself from the proud
God favors the proud rather than the lowly
God ignores both the proud and the lowly
God only respects the strong and powerful
questions.correctAnswer: God respects the lowly but distances Himself from the proud
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:6 teaches that God has respect for the humble and lowly, but He knows the proud from afar, encouraging believers to embrace humility.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:5 teach about the motivation for singing in the ways of the LORD?
options: Because the LORD's glory is great
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD's glory is great
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:5 explains that the great glory of the LORD motivates people to sing in His ways, emphasizing worship as a response to God's greatness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:4 indicates that the LORD's words will only be praised by the kings of Israel.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:4 states 'All the kings of the earth' will praise the LORD, indicating a universal scope beyond just Israel's kings.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 138:6, God is indifferent to the pride of individuals and treats everyone equally.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:6 clearly distinguishes how God respects the lowly but knows the proud from afar, showing He does not treat everyone equally in this regard.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:7 teaches that even in trouble, the LORD will strengthen and save those who trust in Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:7 states that though the believer walks in trouble, the LORD will revive and save them, showing His sustaining power.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:8 promise will happen to the works of the LORD's own hands?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8 assures that the LORD will not forsake the works of His own hands, reflecting His enduring commitment to His creation.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 138 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 138.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:7, what does the psalmist claim God will do when he walks in the midst of trouble?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:7 states, 'Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou wilt revive me,' indicating that God restores and strengthens the psalmist during difficult times.

questions.question: What is the significance of 'thy right hand' in Psalms 138:7 within the context of biblical symbolism?
options: It symbolizes God's power and salvation
It refers to a physical hand
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes God's power and salvation
questions.explanation: In Psalms 138:7, 'thy right hand shall save me' uses the right hand as a biblical symbol of God's power and deliverance, a theme echoed in Exodus 15:6 where God's right hand is mighty.

questions.question: Which phrase in Psalms 138:8 indicates the psalmist's confidence in God's enduring mercy?
options: The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me
Forsake not the works of thine own hands
Thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever
Thou shalt stretch forth thine hand
questions.correctAnswer: Thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8 clearly states, 'thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever,' highlighting the everlasting nature of God's mercy as the foundation of the psalmist's confidence.

questions.question: The psalmist's statement 'The LORD will perfect that which concerneth me' in Psalms 138:8 most closely relates to which New Testament passage emphasizing God's work in believers?
questions.explanation: Philippians 1:6 says God 'will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ,' paralleling Psalms 138:8's assurance that God perfects what concerns the believer.

questions.question: In Psalms 138:7, the phrase 'thou shalt stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies' demonstrates which literary device?
questions.explanation: The phrase personifies God's hand as an active agent against enemies, a common biblical device to depict divine intervention (Psalms 138:7).

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'revive' in Psalms 138:7 (חָיַה, chayah) primarily means:
options: To bring back to life or restore vitality
questions.correctAnswer: To bring back to life or restore vitality
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root חָיַה (chayah) means 'to live' or 'to revive,' indicating restoration of life or strength as reflected in Psalms 138:7.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event is thematically echoed by the psalmist's confidence that God will 'stretch forth thine hand against the wrath of mine enemies' in Psalms 138:7?
options: The parting of the Red Sea
The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: The parting of the Red Sea
questions.explanation: The imagery of God's hand acting against enemies recalls Exodus 14:21 where God stretches out His hand to part the Red Sea and defeat the Egyptians, paralleling Psalms 138:7.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:8 contains an inclusio by mentioning 'the works of thine own hands' which frames the psalmist's trust in God's creation and providence.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8 ends with 'forsake not the works of thine own hands,' creating an inclusio that brackets the psalmist's trust in God's faithful care over His creation and people.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:6, how does God relate to the proud compared to the lowly?
options: He honors the proud and ignores the lowly
He respects the lowly but knows the proud from afar
He loves the proud more than the lowly
questions.correctAnswer: He respects the lowly but knows the proud from afar
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:6 states, 'Though the LORD be high, yet hath he respect unto the lowly: but the proud he knoweth afar off,' showing God's favor towards humility.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God honoring the lowly and opposing the proud as seen in Psalms 138:6?
questions.explanation: James 4:6 quotes, 'God resisteth the proud, but giveth grace unto the humble,' reflecting the theme in Psalms 138:6.

questions.question: What does the psalmist mean by 'thy word' being magnified above all thy name in Psalms 138:2?
options: God's promises and decrees are supreme and trustworthy
God's physical name is more important
questions.correctAnswer: God's promises and decrees are supreme and trustworthy
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 says, 'thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name,' emphasizing the supreme value and reliability of God's promises over even the reputation of His name.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 138:3 shows that God responded specifically on the day the psalmist cried out with strengthened soul.
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 states, 'In the day when I cried thou answeredst me, and strengthenedst me with strength in my soul,' but it does not specify it was the same day, only that God answered when he cried.

questions.question: Psalms 138:4-5 speak of kings praising God when they hear His words. This theme is most closely related to which prophetic passage about nations coming to God's light?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 60:3 says 'The Gentiles shall come to thy light, and kings to the brightness of thy rising,' paralleling the universal praise in Psalms 138:4-5.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes the overall literary structure of Psalms 138, considering the themes of praise, God's faithfulness, and His protection?
options: Chiasm with praise framing God's protection and mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm with praise framing God's protection and mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 138 exhibits a chiasm where initial praise (verses 1-2) frames the middle focus on God's protection and mercy (verses 7-8), highlighting the inseparability of worship and trust.

questions.question: How does the theme of God's enduring mercy in Psalms 138:8 develop the idea of covenant faithfulness found earlier in the Old Testament?
options: It affirms God's everlasting covenant love
It introduces a new covenant unrelated to the past
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms God's everlasting covenant love
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8’s 'thy mercy, O LORD, endureth for ever' echoes covenant promises like those in Exodus 34:6-7 emphasizing God's steadfast love and faithfulness.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 138 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 138 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: According to Psalms 138:1, what motivates David to praise God with his whole heart?
options: Before the gods he will sing praise
questions.correctAnswer: Before the gods he will sing praise
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:1 states that David will praise God with his whole heart and sing before the gods, indicating his wholehearted worship in the presence of other spiritual beings.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:2 declare God has magnified above all His name?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:2 clearly says that God has magnified His word above all His name, emphasizing the supreme importance of God's promises and truth.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by God answering and strengthening the soul when David cried out, according to Psalms 138:3?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 shows God's faithfulness in responding to David's cries and strengthening him, reflecting God's reliable covenantal character (cf. Lamentations 3:22-23).

questions.question: What universal response is foretold in Psalms 138:4 concerning the kings of the earth?
options: They will seek the Lord's counsel
They shall praise the Lord when they hear His words
They shall wage war against the Lord's people
questions.correctAnswer: They shall praise the Lord when they hear His words
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:4 prophesies that all kings will praise the Lord upon hearing His words, indicating the universal acknowledgment of God's authority.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is highlighted in Psalms 138:6 where He has respect for the lowly but knows the proud from afar?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:6 reveals God's justice in how He honors the humble but distances Himself from the proud, reflecting divine righteousness (cf. James 4:6).

questions.question: How does Psalms 138:7 describe God's saving action amid trouble?
options: By reviving the soul and stretching out His hand against enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By reviving the soul and stretching out His hand against enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:7 teaches that God revives the believer even in trouble and actively intervenes against enemies, demonstrating His protective salvation.

questions.question: What eternal quality of God is affirmed in Psalms 138:8 that assures the believer of ongoing mercy?
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8 states that God's mercy endures forever, affirming the eternal nature of divine compassion and covenantal faithfulness (cf. Exodus 34:6).

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Psalms 138:2 and 138:8 teach about God's word and mercy?
options: God's word is temporary but mercy is eternal
God's word is magnified because His mercy endures forever
God's mercy is shown only to the proud
questions.correctAnswer: God's word is magnified because His mercy endures forever
questions.explanation: Together, Psalms 138:2 and 138:8 emphasize that God's word is exalted above all because it is backed by His eternal mercy, revealing the inseparable link between divine truth and lovingkindness.

questions.question: How do Psalms 138:4-5 and Psalms 138:6 together illustrate God's relationship to earthly rulers and the humble?
options: God ignores rulers and only cares for the humble
God punishes rulers who do not humble themselves and blesses the humble
All kings will praise God, and God honors the lowly while distancing from the proud
God elevates the proud as rulers
questions.correctAnswer: All kings will praise God, and God honors the lowly while distancing from the proud
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:4-5 predicts universal praise from kings, while 138:6 teaches that God respects the lowly but knows the proud from afar, showing divine justice and sovereignty.

questions.question: What does Psalms 138:1-2 combined teach about the nature of worship and the priority of God's attributes?
options: Worship is only about feelings, not God's attributes
Worship should be wholehearted and focuses on God's word and truth above His name
Worship is directed only to angels
Worship is to be silent and private
questions.correctAnswer: Worship should be wholehearted and focuses on God's word and truth above His name
questions.explanation: Verses 1-2 show David's wholehearted praise and worship directed toward God's holy temple, emphasizing God's word and truth as paramount over even His name.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is distant and indifferent to human suffering. What does Psalms 138:3 and 138:7 actually teach about God's involvement in human trouble?
options: God answers and strengthens the soul in trouble and actively saves from enemies
God is unaware of individual troubles
questions.correctAnswer: God answers and strengthens the soul in trouble and actively saves from enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:3 and 138:7 affirm that God responds to cries for help, strengthens the soul, revives in trouble, and saves from enemies, refuting claims of divine indifference.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by Psalms 138:8 regarding God's work in the life of the believer?
options: Divine providence perfecting what concerns the believer
questions.correctAnswer: Divine providence perfecting what concerns the believer
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:8 teaches that the Lord will perfect all things concerning the believer, demonstrating God's providential care and ongoing sanctification.

questions.question: What theological truth is highlighted by the contrast in Psalms 138:6 between God's respect for the lowly and His knowledge of the proud from afar?
options: God's special election based on merit
God's justice and holiness in relation to human pride and humility
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and holiness in relation to human pride and humility
questions.explanation: This verse reveals God's just and holy nature, honoring humility while opposing pride, consistent with biblical themes of divine judgment (cf. Proverbs 3:34).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most directly displayed in Psalms 138:2’s statement that He has magnified His word above all His name?
questions.explanation: Magnifying His word above His name highlights God's commitment to truth and faithfulness in His promises (cf. John 17:17).

questions.question: How does Psalms 138:5 contribute to the biblical narrative of God's glory in relation to human praise?
options: It shows that God's glory is hidden from all
It states that human praise is unnecessary
It reveals that kings and people will sing in the ways of the Lord because His glory is great
It claims God's glory is only for angels
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals that kings and people will sing in the ways of the Lord because His glory is great
questions.explanation: Psalms 138:5 connects human praise with recognition of God's great glory, fitting the biblical theme of worship as the response to divine majesty.
